Source-level paid resource ledger

This candidate deliberately exposes a conservative finite-bit account rather
than a speed or RAM benchmark. The ledger is constructed internally, retained
through validation, C reconstruction, digest checks, normalization, immutable
construction and the exact guard. No supplied free/prepaid receipt is accepted.

Every reached exact input integer is read at magnitude width max(1,bit_length
of its absolute value), plus a sign bit in input_integer_bits. Its value is
recorded before width or numerical-domain rejection. Rejections retain this
prefix snapshot. Exact-type rejection does not pretend to read a noninteger's
payload as a valid integer. Rejected strings have their length charged; the
encoding check and fixed tags operate only after the text cap check.

For each integer record with input/output magnitude widths w_1,...,w_s, charge
32*(2+sum_i w_i)^2 bit operations, one produced integer of output width+1, and
an event. This dominates ordinary schoolbook operations on the listed exact
finite integers. Comparisons, branches, sign/absolute-value work, shift-count
work, index/path construction, bounded loops and bookkeeping are covered by
the separate control envelope below; they are not described as free work.

The byte account charges canonical binary encodings, SHA-256 streaming and
fixed-length hex output. byte_work_units counts encoded/processed byte units;
8192*byte_work_units is included in the work upper bound. Fixed SHA state and
padding, encoding temporary copies and byte processing control are dominated
by this constant and the control/storage envelopes. This assumes the standard
finite fixed-round SHA-256 algorithm, not an arbitrary replacement hash.
Output hashing does not certify ALG034 and is separate from archive sealing.

Let A be the summed integer arithmetic charge, I the summed produced signed
integer bits, J the explicit allocated slots, Z the byte units, and Q the
maximum reached integer width (including an eventual rejected width). Let
E=256+sum of all event counts except the byte_processing multiplicity; byte
operation counts themselves are retained. Define H=Q+bit_length(E)+2. Return:
  bookkeeping_work_upper = 1024 E H^2
  total_bit_work_upper = A + 1024 E H^2 + 8192 Z
  cumulative_storage_upper_bits = I + 1024 E H + 8 Z.

All allocations increment an event and are included in E. Numeric record
calls each increment an event. Input and output copies, newly produced integer
bits, temporary encodings, all diagnostic receipt/contract fields and bounded
bookkeeping are upper-bounded cumulatively, not hidden as free input storage.
The fixed 256 setup envelope pays the small record and return constructors.
Python object headers, allocator behavior, garbage collection, executable
loading, real wall time, kernel I/O and physical random access are not claimed
to be modeled. Existing caller payload storage is input storage; the newly
constructed Q16 source is separately paid in this combined pipeline.

Actual successful nonzero pass inventory

- Certificate parser: five exact tags, two digest strings, ten integer fields.
- Exact C reconstruction: B_A binomial steps, explicit min comparison, bounded
  power-of-two construction and integer products; this repeats/validates the
  upstream planning formula, so it is an additional paid cost here.
- First dense pass: N cell checks, 2N exact numerator reads, squares/additions,
  canonical encodings and streaming digest updates.
- Second dense pass: 2N already validated source reads, 2N nearest-even rounds,
  and 2N new squared terms, with N temporary immutable rounded pairs.
- Final pass: 2N scaled numerators, Cartesian checks and squared terms; 4N
  dyadic field writes; N complex-cell writes; N outer immutable tuple copies.
- Exact source header and scalar scale/allowance construction remain charged.

The explicit allocated slot calls total 21N+60 on a successful nonzero path:
2 initial; 34 copied certificate fields/temporaries; 3(2+2N) integer-encoding
scratch slots; 1 digest output; N+4N rounded temporary slots; N output-list
slots; 6N Cartesian tuple/list slots; 2N complex tuple slots; N+2 final source
slots; 15 result slots. All of these copies are in the same cumulative account.

The exact-zero or zero-approximation path avoids second/final passes but still
pays the complete dense validation and digest, plus any applicable nonzero
C reconstruction. Invalid paths stop at their reached validation prefix; their
receipt is preserved even when an oversized final coordinate is rejected.

For a readable conservative asymptotic envelope, write q for the maximum
accepted numerator width, D for the maximum metadata encoding width, and
M=N. Pq and F are O(log M). Binomial intermediates have O(M) bits for B_A<=M.
All numerical widths are O(q+M+D), except that actual rejected input widths
replace the corresponding q or D in a failure-prefix account. The number of
nonbyte events is O(M+B_A) and the byte volume is O(Mq+D). Consequently a
conservative successful-call source-model work bound is
  O((M+B_A)*(q+M+D+log(M+2))^2 + Mq+D),
with cumulative produced/storage envelope of the corresponding linear-width
form O((M+B_A)*(q+M+D+log(M+2)) + Mq+D).
These deliberately loose bounds include recomputing C and all bookkeeping.
They do not claim the earlier mathematical bridge's sharper minimal ledger.

Retained numerical output is O(M*(F+log(F+2))) bits plus tuple/address storage,
producer metadata, scale exponent and the fixed-size event/receipt structure.
Temporary storage and destroyed values remain in the cumulative ledger.
The full upstream producer ledger is additional. Actual Q16 window/root/scale
preparation, all bucket calls, decoder/phase/median work, supplied schedules,
rational sparse-parameter widths and external I/O remain additional too.
Nothing in this wrapper changes the accepted Q16 cost or supplies a sub-FFT,
full-recovery or practical-performance theorem.
